title: Rav Tachlifa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Moed Katan 25a he said: “I saw Rav Huna wishing to sit on his bed,” etc. But the statement is cited in Menachot 32b, and there it is Rav Chelbo, Hyman reports the same reading in Yuchasin and Dikdukei Soferim.
We find at the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat, chapter 2: Rabbi Tachlifa asked Rav Chisda, “Did you not, Master, teach us thus?” etc.
In Avodah Zarah 15a: Rav Tachlifa said that Rav Shila bar Avimi (or Avina) said in Rav’s name.
In Jerusalem Talmud Peah 4:7: a dispute of Rav Kahana and Rabbi Tachlifa.

notes.text: Saved Davidson Moed Katan 25a fully writes Rav Huna and concerns sitting on his bed. The Shabbat chapter/halakhah locator is Jerusalem Talmud, where רבי in the address to Rav Chisda is rendered “Master,” not automatically the proper name Rabbi.
